public_rationale: The speaker said losses 'appear to be' mounting at a dramatic rate, based on the figures he reported. Tested on those terms, the claim holds. The Financial Times checked the audited figures separately and reports OpenAI's net loss rose from about $5 billion in 2024 to about $39 billion in 2025, roughly 7.8 times. That is a dramatic rise on the headline figure he cited. One caveat matters: the FT says most of the rise came from a one-time non-cash charge tied to OpenAI's restructuring. Without it and other non-cash items, the 2025 loss was about $8 billion. On that basis growth was much smaller. His remark about sustainability and profitability is opinion and is not graded.
limitations: The figures come from leaked audited statements verified by the FT, not from a public OpenAI filing.
The headline net-loss rise is driven mostly by a non-recurring non-cash charge. An underlying-loss reading would show much slower growth.
Only two years of data were reported.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's losses appear to be growing dramatically year over year.

statement.excerpt: Losses also appear to be mounting year-over-year at a dramatic rate, and I’m not sure how this company finds a way toward any kind of sustainability or profitability.
statement.document_title: Exclusive: OpenAI Losses Increased Nearly 8X in 2025, With Spending Hitting $34 Billion

from_speaker: context: "$38.53 billion in losses" for 2025, from audited documents
"I'm not sure how this company finds a way toward any kind of sustainability or profitability" (opinion, not graded)
our_interpretation: The speaker hedges with "appear to be". That hedge rests on the 2024 and 2025 figures he had just reported. So the fair test is narrow. Do the reported annual figures show OpenAI's losses rising sharply from 2024 to 2025? I do not treat the hedge as a firmer claim than he made.
The measure is OpenAI's net loss attributable to the company, the figure he cites, for calendar 2025 compared with calendar 2024.
"Dramatic" has its plain meaning: a large multiple, far beyond ordinary growth. A rise of several times would meet it. A small or flat change would not.
The second clause, about sustainability and profitability, states uncertainty and opinion. It is not graded.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reporting of OpenAI's audited or company figures shows its 2025 net loss was several times its 2024 net loss.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible figures show OpenAI's 2025 net loss was flat, lower, or only modestly higher than in 2024.
